basic_information.short_title: Creation of the Municipality of Kadayangan
basic_information.official_title: AN ACT CREATING THE MUNICIPALITY OF KADAYANGAN, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
signed_by: Prof. Raby B. Angkal, Secretary General
basic_information.effectivity: 15 days after publication in the Bangsamoro Gazette or one newspaper of regional circulation

citizen_summary.what_is_this_about: Creates the Municipality of Kadayangan in the Special Geographic Area from 7 barangays of Midsayap, North Cotabato — barangays that petitioned and voted to join the Bangsamoro in the 2019 plebiscite.
citizen_summary.why_was_it_proposed: Those barangays voted themselves into the BARMM in 2019 but remained attached to municipalities outside it. This act gives them a municipality of their own inside the region.
citizen_summary.what_will_change: If ratified, the 7 barangays become a distinct and independent municipality seated at Barangay Kapinpilan, with first officials appointed with due regard to women's representation and monthly financial assistance until its national tax share arrives.
who_will_be_affected: Residents of the 7 barangays, who vote in the plebiscite
Midsayap, North Cotabato — the mother municipality, which sit outside the BARMM
Women of the Bangsamoro, whose representation must be considered in the first appointments
citizen_summary.when_will_it_take_effect: The act is in force, but corporate existence depends on ratification in a plebiscite within 60 days of approval.

what_this_means_for_you.in_short: You decide. This creates the Municipality of Kadayangan from 7 barangays that voted to join the Bangsamoro in 2019 — but it only exists if a majority of voters there approve it in a plebiscite.
in_practice: 7 barangays separate from their mother municipality: Central Labas, Kapinpilan, Malingao, Mudseng, Sambulawan, Tugal, Tumbras
They become the Municipality of Kadayangan in the Special Geographic Area of the BARMM
The seat of government is Barangay Kapinpilan
The territorial boundary follows the existing boundaries of the constituent barangays
A plebiscite decides it within 60 days of approval, conducted by COMELEC through the Bangsamoro Electoral Office
The Chief Minister appoints the first mayor, vice-mayor and eight Sangguniang Bayan members, with due regard to representation of women of the Bangsamoro
Monthly financial assistance from the Bangsamoro Government until the municipality receives its national tax allotment share

for_specific_groups.Voters in the barangays concerned: You already voted to join the Bangsamoro in 2019. This vote decides whether you become a municipality of your own within it.
for_specific_groups.Women: Section 7 requires the first appointments to be made with due regard to the representation of women of the Bangsamoro.
for_specific_groups.Incumbent councillors of Midsayap: If you actually reside in the new municipality, you serve out your remaining term in the mother municipality.
for_specific_groups.Everyone else: No duty falls on the public.

what_this_means_for_you.where_this_applies: The Special Geographic Area of the BARMM — 7 barangays formerly of Midsayap, North Cotabato.
what_you_can_do: Check whether your barangay is among the 7 named in Section 2
Ask the Bangsamoro Electoral Office when it is scheduled
watch_out_for: The act states no peso figure for the monthly financial assistance — only that it shall be provided every month.
The first set of municipal officials is appointed by the Chief Minister, not elected.
As enacted, the plebiscite is confined to the barangays comprising the new municipality.
No population figure and no land area are stated in the operative sections.

key_terms_explained.Special Geographic Area: The barangays of North Cotabato that voted in the 2019 plebiscite to join the BARMM, now being organised into municipalities of the region.
key_terms_explained.Plebiscite: A vote of the people affected, required before a municipality can be created.
key_terms_explained.National Tax Allotment: A local government's share of national taxes, formerly the Internal Revenue Allotment.

what_this_means_for_you.status_note: Passed Safar 1, 1445 / 17 August 2023, approved by the Chief Minister on 4 September 2023.

benefits.headline: A municipality of their own for barangays that voted into the Bangsamoro in 2019.

direct_benefits.benefit: A local government inside the region rather than attachment to a municipality outside it
direct_benefits.how_to_access: Subject to ratification in the plebiscite

direct_benefits.benefit: Monthly financial assistance until the national tax share arrives
direct_benefits.who_gets_it: The new Municipal Government of Kadayangan

direct_benefits.benefit: Consideration of women's representation in the first appointments

indirect_benefits: Entitlement to a share of national taxes once allocated
limitations: Nothing takes effect without a favourable plebiscite.
The first officials are appointed, not elected.
No amount is stated for the monthly assistance.

for_citizens: None beyond voting in the plebiscite, which is a right rather than a duty.

what_is_prohibited: The act defines no prohibited acts and creates no offences.

penalties.for_citizens: None. The act creates no offence, fine or imprisonment.

where_to_complain.first_stop: Commission on Elections, through the Bangsamoro Electoral Office, which conducts and supervises the plebiscite
where_to_complain.oversight: Office of the Chief Minister, which appoints the first municipal officials
where_to_complain.note: The act creates no complaints procedure of its own.

everyday_scenarios: A resident of Barangay Central Labas voted in 2019 to join the Bangsamoro but has remained under a municipality outside the region. This act would put them in a municipality inside it — subject to a further vote.
A sitting councillor of Midsayap who lives in one of the 7 barangays finishes their term serving the mother municipality, not the new one.

key_provisions: Section 1 — Policy: the Bangsamoro Government may create, divide, merge, abolish or substantially alter the boundaries of municipalities or barangays by act of Parliament, with units so created entitled to their appropriate share in the national tax allotment, provided the change is approved by a majority of the votes cast in a plebiscite in the political units directly affected.

Section 2 — Separates the barangays of Central Labas, Kapinpilan, Malingao, Mudseng, Sambulawan, Tugal, Tumbras, belonging to the Municipality of Midsayap, North Cotabato, which petitioned and voted to be included in the BARMM in the 2019 plebiscite, and constitutes them into the distinct and independent Municipality of Kadayangan, Special Geographic Area of the BARMM.
Section 3 — The seat of government is Barangay Kapinpilan.
Section 4 — The territorial boundary follows the existing boundaries of the constituent barangays.

Section 5 — The municipality acquires corporate existence on ratification by a majority of the votes cast by qualified voters in a plebiscite in those barangays, held within 60 days after approval of the act.

Section 6 — The Commission on Elections, through the Bangsamoro Electoral Office, conducts and supervises the plebiscite, with expenses taken from the current fiscal year appropriations of the Bangsamoro Government.

Section 7 — The first mayor, vice-mayor and eight Sangguniang Bayan members are appointed by the Chief Minister with due regard to representation of women of the Bangsamoro, and hold office until successors are elected at the next general elections for local officials. Incumbent elective Sangguniang Bayan members of the mother municipality who actually reside in the new municipality serve out their remaining terms there.

Section 8 — The Bangsamoro Government shall appropriate and provide financial assistance for the administration and operation of the Municipal Government of Kadayangan every month until it is allocated its share in the national tax allotment.
Section 11 — Takes effect 15 days after publication in the Bangsamoro Gazette or one newspaper of regional circulation.

who_benefits: Residents of the 7 Special Geographic Area barangays
Women of the Bangsamoro, through the appointment provision
impact.allocated_budget: Monthly financial assistance, amount not stated; plebiscite costs from the current fiscal year appropriations.
impact.figures_note: The act states no peso amount, no land area and no population figure.

related_legislation.related_note: One of seven municipalities created in the Special Geographic Area on 17 August 2023, with BAA 41 (Pahamuddin), 42 (Kadayangan), 43 (Nabalawag), 44 (Old Kaabakan), 45 (Kapalawan), 46 (Malidegao) and 47 (Tugunan), organising the North Cotabato barangays that voted to join the BARMM in the 2019 plebiscite.

implementation_status.note: Read from the enacted text as signed. Whether the plebiscite was held, and what it decided, is not recorded here.

citizen_questions.q: What is the Special Geographic Area?
citizen_questions.a: The barangays of North Cotabato that petitioned and voted in the 2019 plebiscite to be included in the BARMM. Seven acts passed on the same day organise them into municipalities of the region.
Central Labas, Kapinpilan, Malingao, Mudseng, Sambulawan, Tugal, Tumbras — formerly of Midsayap, North Cotabato.
Not until a plebiscite ratifies it, to be held within 60 days of the act's approval and run by COMELEC through the Bangsamoro Electoral Office.

citizen_questions.q: How much financial assistance is there?
citizen_questions.a: The act says monthly assistance shall be provided until the national tax allotment share is allocated, but states no amount — unlike the Maguindanao creation acts of December 2023, which specify not less than ₱2.5 million a month.

citizen_questions.q: Who will be the first mayor?
citizen_questions.a: Whoever the Chief Minister appoints, with due regard to the representation of women of the Bangsamoro. The first officials serve until the next general elections for local officials.
